title: Front Street Taproom
venue_description:
About Front Street Taproom

Front Street Taproom stands as downtown Fargo's premier craft beer destination, showcasing the impressive brewing talent of the Fargo-Moorhead area and surrounding region. With an unwavering commitment to supporting local small businesses, all 30 taps feature locally brewed beer from Minnesota, North Dakota, South Dakota, and Wisconsin breweries.

The Venue Experience

Located on historic Main Avenue (formerly Front Street), the taproom offers a warm and inviting atmosphere with rustic wooden decor, comfortable seating across two levels, and a spacious mezzanine that can accommodate up to 35 people for private events. The venue welcomes well-behaved small dogs and maintains a community-focused atmosphere perfect for conversation and connection.

Music & Entertainment

Front Street Taproom has established itself as an important venue for Fargo's creative community. Monday nights feature open mic hosted by Travis Neros, welcoming all forms of creative expression including music, readings, comedy, and poetry. Sign-up begins at 7:30 PM with the event running from 8:00 PM to 11:00 PM. The venue also hosts trivia nights, vinyl listening parties, and live music on weekends.

The Cellar - Comedy Venue

Below the taproom lies The Cellar, an underground comedy club that brings professional touring comedians to Fargo. This intimate 100-person capacity space hosts regular comedy shows with both local and national acts. The unique basement setting creates an authentic comedy club atmosphere rarely found in North Dakota.

Food & Drink

While the taproom does not have a kitchen, guests are welcome to bring their own food or order delivery from neighboring restaurants. Rhombus Guys, voted Best Pizza in Fargo seven years running, delivers their full menu to the taproom at no extra charge. The bar features an impressive rotating selection of craft beers, ciders, wines, seltzers, kombucha, and non-alcoholic beverages.

Private Events

The venue offers two spaces for private rentals: the Mezzanine (up to 35 people) and The Cellar (up to 100 people). These spaces are perfect for birthdays, rehearsal dinners, company functions, fundraisers, showers, and meetings. Guests can bring their own food and enjoy affordable hourly rates.

Hours & Location

The taproom opens daily at 4:00 PM, staying open until 11:00 PM Monday through Thursday and until midnight on Friday and Saturday. Daily happy hour specials make it an ideal after-work destination. Plentiful street parking is available, and a parking depot across the street on Broadway offers free parking during business hours.

title: Troll Lounge at Sons of Norway
venue_description:
About the Troll Lounge

The Troll Lounge represents one of Fargo's most distinctive and culturally rich music venues. Located inside the Sons of Norway Kringen Lodge, this unique bar features hand-carved wooden trolls and Norwegian murals that transport visitors to a different world. The venue has earned a reputation as a must-visit destination for both locals and visitors seeking an authentic cultural experience combined with quality live music.

The Sons of Norway Connection

Kringen Lodge 425, established in the Fargo-Moorhead area, is part of Sons of Norway, the largest Norwegian organization outside Norway. The lodge strives to promote and preserve Norwegian culture and heritage through food, activities, education, and events. The current location at 722 2nd Avenue North, just south of NDSU's business school, opened to provide a modern home for this historic organization.

Music Programming

The Troll Lounge hosts weekly live music events featuring diverse genres including rock, folk, country, bluegrass, and traditional Norwegian music. Tuesday evenings bring the bluegrass jam session from 6:00 PM to 8:00 PM, where musicians are encouraged to bring their instruments and join in collaborative picking. This free, all-levels-welcome jam creates community among acoustic music enthusiasts.

Monthly Amped Open Mic nights, hosted by Amped School of Music, occur on Thursday evenings starting at 7:30 PM. These events welcome music, comedy, and poetry performances in a supportive, low-pressure environment. Professional backline equipment including keyboards, drums, guitars, and ukuleles are available on stage for performers. Each month features themed songs and community song challenges to encourage participation and skill development.

The Venue Atmosphere

What sets the Troll Lounge apart is its authentic Norwegian atmosphere. Hand-carved trolls peer from various corners of the room, and traditional Norwegian murals adorn the walls. The signature drink is aquavit, a Norwegian spirit available in multiple varieties including dill, citron, and caraway flavors. Norwegian beers like Aass Pilsner complement the cultural experience.

The intimate setting provides excellent acoustics for live performances while maintaining the character of a traditional Norwegian gathering place. Happy hour runs from 4:30 PM to 6:00 PM with $1 off all drinks, making it an attractive pre-show option for early arrivals.

Kringen Kafé

Adjacent to the Troll Lounge, the Kringen Kafé serves authentic Scandinavian-American cuisine Tuesday through Friday. Morning service from 9:00 AM to 11:00 AM features coffee, caramel rolls, and pastries. Lunch runs from 11:00 AM to 1:30 PM with made-from-scratch entrees, soups, and desserts. Popular menu items include the Lefse Crunch Burger, Troll Burger with mushroom and Swiss, Philly Cheesesteak, Fish and Chips, and Norwegian specialties.

Cultural Events & Programs

Beyond music, the Sons of Norway Kringen Lodge hosts various cultural programs, classes, and member activities. The organization publishes the monthly Kringen Posten newsletter celebrating Norwegian-American heritage, featuring cultural programs, member spotlights, and volunteer opportunities. The venue welcomes both lodge members and the general public to experience Norwegian culture.

Venue Policies

The Troll Lounge is a 21+ venue with special accommodations for young performers. Individuals under 18 must be accompanied by a parent, and adults ages 18-20 are only permitted in the bar when performing. This policy ensures a welcoming environment for emerging artists while maintaining appropriate venue standards.

Location & Accessibility

Situated in downtown Fargo at 722 2nd Avenue North, the Sons of Norway building is easily accessible from NDSU and the surrounding downtown area. The historic building combines cultural authenticity with modern amenities, creating a unique gathering place unlike any other in the region.

title: Hope and Coffee
venue_description:
About Hope and Coffee

Hope and Coffee holds the distinction of being Fargo's first nonprofit coffee shop, operating under the mission of Soul Solutions Recovery Center. This unique establishment demonstrates that a coffee shop can be more than just a place to grab a beverage – it can be a transformative community space that supports recovery, fosters creativity, and brings people together regardless of their background or journey.

Mission & Inspiration

Inspired by the original Hope and Coffee café in Pennsylvania, this Fargo location was founded to normalize recovery and provide a safe, welcoming environment where those in recovery and the general public can merge together. All proceeds from the coffee shop support the broader mission of helping each individual find recovery and embrace their best life. The philosophy recognizes that life can be rough for everyone, and this communal space offers support, connection, and acceptance.

Music & Open Mic

Every Saturday evening from 7:00 PM to 9:00 PM, Hope and Coffee hosts Open Expressions, an acoustic open mic night presented by Wagon Works. Sign-up begins at 6:00 PM for this family-friendly event that welcomes all forms of creative expression. Musicians, poets, spoken word artists, and performers of all kinds find a supportive platform to share their talents.

The open mic is completely free to attend and participate in, with no cover charge. Professional PA system, microphones, and cables are provided for performers. The all-genres, all-ages format ensures that everyone can participate regardless of musical style or experience level. This weekly gathering has become an important part of Fargo's creative community, providing consistent performance opportunities in a substance-free environment.

Additional Events

Beyond open mic nights, Hope and Coffee hosts a diverse calendar of community events. Sober Karaoke nights offer the brave an opportunity to showcase their vocal talents with lights, mics, amps, and access to YouTube's vast music library. The venue regularly schedules movie nights, art-centric classes, crafting sessions, and various workshops designed to engage the community in healthy, creative activities.

The Coffee Shop Experience

The 1,300 square foot space provides comfortable seating for conversation, relaxation, watching sports, playing cards or trivia, or reading. Free Wi-Fi ensures guests can work or browse while enjoying their beverages. The menu features excellent coffee, lattes, smoothies, sodas, and baked goods – all prepared with care and served in a welcoming atmosphere.

Recovery Bookstore

Inside the shop, visitors find the Recovery Bookstore offering books, resources, and support materials related to recovery and personal growth. This integrated resource ensures that those seeking information or support can access it in a comfortable, non-judgmental environment while enjoying a cup of coffee.

Community Center

An attached community center expands the venue's programming capabilities, offering classes and activities for everyone. This additional space allows Hope and Coffee to serve as more than just a coffee shop – it functions as a comprehensive community resource center focused on wellness, creativity, and connection.

Hours & Accessibility

The coffee shop operates from 8:00 AM to 8:00 PM on weekdays, providing ample time for morning coffee runs, afternoon study sessions, and evening events. The Tuesday loyalty program offers double punches on the free punch card for every specialty drink ordered, encouraging regular visits and community building.

Location Details

Located at 1801 38th Street South in Fargo, the venue can be a bit tricky to find on first visit. Traveling south on 38th Street SW (the frontage road west of the I-29 southbound exit to westbound I-94), visitors turn right into the parking lot at 1801. The large yellow brick building houses the recovery center, with Hope and Coffee's entrance on the west side of the building. Look around the corner from the front signage to locate the door.

Philosophy & Impact

Hope and Coffee represents a powerful model of how businesses can serve dual purposes – providing quality products while advancing important social missions. By creating a space where recovery is normalized and celebrated, where creativity is encouraged, and where all community members are genuinely welcome, the venue has established itself as an essential part of Fargo's social infrastructure. The combination of substance-free entertainment, supportive community, and quality refreshments demonstrates that meaningful social spaces don't require alcohol to thrive.

title: The Aquarium

About The Aquarium

Since opening in 2006, The Aquarium has established itself as North Dakota's premier live music venue. Located in the heart of downtown Fargo above Dempsey's Public House, this independently owned and operated venue has hosted more national, regional, and local bands and artists than any other place in the state. With a capacity of 260 people, The Aquarium offers an intimate concert experience that has attracted some of the biggest names in independent music.

Notable Performances

The venue's impressive history includes performances by Father John Misty, Bon Iver, Phoebe Bridgers, The Melvins, Prof, Built To Spill, Band of Horses, Trampled By Turtles, Against Me!, Screaming Females, and hundreds of other acclaimed acts. This remarkable lineup demonstrates The Aquarium's ability to attract cutting-edge talent across multiple genres including indie rock, folk, punk, metal, hip-hop, and electronic music.

Venue Mission

The Aquarium's mission focuses on bringing original, cutting-edge music to the Fargo-Moorhead area for the purpose of bolstering a more inspired, diverse, and creative community. This commitment to artistic excellence has made the venue a second home for local musicians and music lovers while establishing Fargo as a legitimate stop on national touring routes.

Management & Awards

Ryan Hoffart and Josie Gereszek serve as the venue's co-directors, overseeing all aspects of programming and operations. Fargo entrepreneurs Bert and Klaus Meyers own The Aquarium.
